scope: isolated synthetic loopback HTTPS; fsync unchanged; no WAN capacity claim; deployment recorded separately
notes: Mixed tests are single trials per version/resource cell, not confidence intervals.
Mixed high-rate reads can skip scheduled issuance; these are distinct from HTTP errors.

In the first four mixed trials, skipped read events retain the original legacy/web label, even for subject schedules; aggregate skipped counts and issued subject latency are accurate. Steady trials fix the classification.

Mixed trials with restart only expose queue counters for the last boot in optional_shutdown; those counters do not prove loss-free logging during the load. Burst and steady trials provide same-boot queue accounting.
Native benchmarks report elapsed time including real filesystem sync; allocation count rises about 14 percent even though allocated bytes are similar.
WAF retains one admission mutex for exact global/client token and concurrency decisions.
Log sequence/hash linkage, state application and Write/Sync remain ordered; independent computation is parallel.
Listings use each thread committed generation rather than one board-wide instantaneous view; deletion/expiry leases remain checked before and during transmission.
